description:
Multidisciplinary team from Uruguay interested in biomedical engineering, human biology, computer science, medicine, and space exploration.

We are interested in developing a practical and user-centered solution for monitoring astronaut health during space missions, combining biomedical concepts, software, data, and space-related technologies.
summary:
Carpincho Orbital is a low-cost neuro-ocular health monitoring prototype designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions. It addresses the health risks associated with altered gravity, focusing on Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), a condition involving visual and structural changes in the eyes and brain observed during and after spaceflight.

The system combines VR-based functional visual assessments, including visual acuity, visual field and ocular motility tests, with a clinical dashboard for monitoring results over time. Astronauts can also manually report symptoms and health observations, while wearable-derived indicators, such as heart rate, activity and sleep patterns, can provide additional physiological context.

By combining functional assessments and health information in one platform, Carpincho Orbital aims to support accessible, repeatable neuro-ocular monitoring and facilitate clinical follow-up throughout space missions. The system does not directly measure intracranial pressure or diagnose SANS.
details:
Project Overview

Carpincho Orbital is a neuro-ocular health monitoring platform designed to support astronaut health during long-duration space missions. Our approach focuses on Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), a spaceflight-related condition associated with visual and structural changes in the eyes and brain.

Altered gravity can cause headward fluid shifts, potentially affecting intracranial fluid dynamics and ocular structures. Since these changes may develop progressively, repeated functional assessments and longitudinal health monitoring are important.

How It Works

The platform combines three complementary sources of health information:

1. VR-Based Visual Assessments

A virtual reality headset provides an accessible interface for guided visual assessments, including:

  • Visual acuity.
  • Visual field evaluation.
  • Ocular motility assessment.

These tests aim to capture functional changes through repeatable assessments during the mission.

2. Wearable Health Monitoring

The system is designed to incorporate physiological indicators from wearable technologies, such as smartwatches. Potential parameters include heart rate, physical activity and sleep patterns, providing additional context for health monitoring.

3. Astronaut Health Reports

Astronauts can manually record symptoms, visual disturbances, headaches and other relevant observations, adding subjective health information to the monitoring process.

Clinical Dashboard

The clinical interface organizes visual assessment results, physiological indicators and self-reported symptoms into a centralized monitoring environment. This allows healthcare professionals to review individual health records, track changes over time and identify findings that may require further clinical evaluation.

Innovation and Impact

Carpincho Orbital combines affordable VR technology, wearable health indicators and digital clinical monitoring into a single workflow. Its main innovation is making functional neuro-ocular assessments more accessible and repeatable without relying exclusively on expensive or specialized diagnostic equipment.

The project aims to support astronaut self-monitoring, improve access to longitudinal health information and assist medical teams in evaluating potential neuro-ocular changes during long-duration missions.

Technology

The prototype consists of a web-based astronaut interface, a clinical dashboard and a VR assessment module. The source code is organized in separate GitHub development branches, and the web application is deployed through Render.

The proposed hardware includes a VR headset and commercially available wearable devices.

Demonstration data, when simulated, are illustrative and do not represent actual astronaut medical records.

Carpincho Orbital is a monitoring and screening support tool, not a direct intracranial pressure measurement device or a diagnostic system.
